newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COYOTES CENTER ROENICK MAY MISS DECIDER AGAINST MIGHTY DUCKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COYOTES CENTER ROENICK MAY MISS DECIDER AGAINST MIGHTY DUCKS.

text.p: Phoenix Coyotes centre Jeremy Roenick, the team's second-leading playoffs scorer, injured his left knee in Sunday's 3-2 overtime loss to the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and may miss Tuesday's decisive seventh game.
Roenick will undergo an MRI, but players and coaches held little hope he would be able to play in Western Conference series finale at Anaheim.
"With J.R. out, we're all going to have to dig a little deeper and come up with a different game plan and play together as a team," right wing Mike Gartner said.
Roenick was injured with 11:27 to go in the second period when he collided knee-to-knee in his own zone with Ducks forward Ted Drury.
Roenick went down immediately and had to be helped to the locker room. He suffered a similar injury last April following a knee-to-knee collision with Dallas defenceman Derian Hatcher.
"We kind of both arrived at the same time," Drury said. "I went to the right, he went to the left and our knees caught. I could tell we clipped each other. He went right down."
Irate Coyotes officials said they would send a videotape of the incident to NHL vice president Brian Burke.
"It's a perfect example of a guy going after one of our top players with no intent but to injure," said general manager Bobby Smith.
"You don't like to see those hits. You think that's a bit of a cheap shot," added Phoenix coach Don Hay.
The 27-year-old Roenick has two goals and four assists in six playoff games after collecting 29 goals and 40 assists in 72 games in his first season with the Coyotes.
"Jeremy is one of the top players in the league and has been fantastic in the playoffs," Ducks forward Paul Kariya said. "So obviously, that's a big hole without him."
